openQuestions: Syllabus wording was written from the known UPSC Sociology syllabus; it should be checked against the current CSE notification, and the Hindi titles against UPSC's official Hindi syllabus.
Some UPSC sub-topics are joined into one node (e.g. soc-p1-07, soc-p2-10, soc-p2-35) to keep each at 1-3 study hours; the owner may prefer finer splits.
Paper 2 has no official unit names beyond its A/B/C sections and numbered sub-headings, so unit names combine the two.
Link slugs such as soc-p2-05-modernization-indian-tradition and gs1/world-history-industrial-revolution are made-up slugs for Claude Code to map.
Andre Beteille's essay 'Sociology and Common Sense' (EPW, 1996) is cited from memory; year and argument are in factsToCheck.
